messages:
support-engineer: FYI escalation from AcmeCorp — nightly deploys failing intermittently after 23:15 UTC, lots of 401s hitting our API.
support-engineer: customer log: `HTTP 401 {"error":"unauthorized_client", "error_description":"invalid audience"}`
acme-contact: reproduced locally with `gitlab-runner exec shell` — first job OK, second job in same pipeline gets 401 after ~70s.
maria: I rolled out the short-lived CI tokens last night (TTL=60s) to reduce blast radius. Did we change any runner caching?
raj: we also added strict `aud` enforcement at auth-proxy level: tokens must have `aud=redwood-ci`.
oliver: our default runner config caches tokens for 120s (`token_cache_seconds = 120` in /etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml), so that would explain the window mismatch.
ci-runner: confirming: runner obtains token once, caches for 120s, reuses across jobs. If TTL < cache window some requests use expired tokens.
support-engineer: repro steps customer provided: 1) push commit 2) start pipeline 3) observe deploy job fail with `x-request-id: 0a1b2c` and 401 at `/v1/deploy`
raj: short-term mitigation: either increase token TTL back to 120s or reduce runner cache to <60s. Which is less risky?
maria: I'd prefer runner change (safer) but can revert TTL for critical customers if needed.
emma: oncall, can you kick a canary: update token_cache_seconds to 30s for 5 runners in us-west-2? @sre-oncall
sre-oncall: starting canary now, updating 5 runners, will watch error rate and deploy success. :eyes:
support-engineer: Acme confirmed canary runner succeeded for one full pipeline, still watching for flakes.
oliver: longer-term fix: ship runner change to honor `exp` in JWT and refresh at 60% of TTL rather than fixed cache. Filing ticket INF-518.
raj: also adding an alias acceptance for legacy tokens (accept `aud: redwood-ci-legacy`) while we roll runners out.
acme-contact: thanks — that workaround helped, please keep us posted; hit this during our peak deploy window.
infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-034 created (P2) — owners: infra, auth, runner.
support-engineer: attaching logs and command outputs to Incident. Will publish postmortem if escalates.
